- Comprehensive manufacturer color charts (flake, metallic, solid, quartz, glitter systems)
- Nationwide network of 70+ authorized XPS dealers for professional installation
- Lifetime warranty on all installed floor systems

## Supported Floor Systems
- Flake Epoxy (vinyl chip broadcast)
- Metallic Epoxy (swirled pearlescent finish)
- Solid Color Epoxy (single-color polyaspartic/epoxy)
- Quartz System (broadcast quartz sand)
- Glitter Epoxy (reflective metallic flakes)
- Polished Concrete
- Stained Concrete (acid stain / dye)

## FAQ

### How much does an epoxy garage floor cost?
A typical 2-car garage (400-500 sq ft) costs between $2,000 and $5,000 depending on the system chosen, floor condition, and location. Use our instant online estimator for a personalized quote.

### How long does installation take?
Most residential garage floor installations are completed in 1-2 days. The floor is ready for light foot traffic in 24 hours and full vehicle traffic in 72 hours.

### How long does an epoxy floor last?
A professionally installed epoxy floor with proper preparation can last 15-20+ years. Xtreme Polishing Systems offers a lifetime warranty on installed systems.

### What is the difference between epoxy and polyaspartic?
Polyaspartic is a type of polyurea that cures faster (can be walked on in 4-6 hours vs 24 hours for epoxy) and has higher UV stability. Epoxy is generally more affordable; polyaspartic is often used as a fast-curing topcoat.

### Do I need to prepare my floor before installation?
Yes — proper surface preparation (grinding, crack repair, moisture testing) is critical for adhesion. Our authorized dealers handle all prep as part of the installation.

### Is a deposit required?
Most authorized dealers require a deposit to schedule installation. The deposit amount varies by project size and is applied toward the total project cost.

### Are epoxy floors slippery?
Epoxy floors can be slippery when wet. Most installers offer anti-slip additives (clear grit or aluminum oxide) for garage floors, especially near entryways.

### What does the warranty cover?
The lifetime warranty covers delamination, peeling, and bubbling of the installed floor system. It does not cover damage from improper maintenance, heavy impacts, or chemical spills.
